# CCRPG — Cognitive-Capacity-Driven RPG

> 🚧 **Under Development** — Core architecture complete. First playable
> (Red stage vertical slice) ready for internal testing. Full 64-cell
> assessment module system implemented with 1,280 items across all 8
> stages.

An assessment-module-driven developmental RPG whose every gameplay
encounter is the gamification of a validated developmental assessment,
whose macro-progression is the eight stages of consciousness (64-cell
module architecture: 8 lines x 8 stages), and whose endgame is the
harvest into 4th-density unity in the canonical Law-of-One framing.
Built personally. Designed to be globally deployable. Adaptive to any
age, any developmental altitude.

---

## What this is

CCRPG is **two things at once**:

1. An assessment-module-driven developmental RPG with narrative arcs,
   immersive gameplay, and a 64-cell module architecture (8 lines of
   intelligence x 8 stages of consciousness). Every encounter is a
   module executing in one of four modes (calibration, encounter,
   practice, shadow work).
2. A **literal cognitive / developmental practice** -- every assessment
   module is a validated developmental exercise that simultaneously
   diagnoses AND heals/evolves the player. The game's progression IS
   the demonstration of integrated growth across all eight lines of
   intelligence.

The vision is documented in `docs/00-vision.md`. The binding build
plan is `UNIFIED-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` at the repo root.

## The four canon decisions

| # | Decision |
|:-:|---|
| 1 | **Law-of-One layer = canon, fully integrated.** Seven energy rays as first-class types; harvest into 4th density as canonical endgame. |
| 2 | **No clinical / IRB ambition.** Commitment to *legitimate* neurological / biological / psychological efficacy via validated tasks and honest telemetry — without regulated medical-device certification. |
| 3 | **Adaptive onboarding for any age, any altitude.** Built personally, deployed globally. |
| 4 | **MVP = modular foundation of everything.** All 8 lines, 8 stages, 7 rays, 4 quadrants registered as modules at MVP launch. Red stage as the first vertical slice. Adding the rest is content drops. |

```
CCRPG/
├── README.md                       <- you are here
├── UNIFIED-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md  <- the binding build plan
├── MVP-BLUEPRINT.md                <- vision & philosophy (implementation details superseded)

│   ├── STAGE-ASSESSMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md <- module contract & execution modes
│   ├── ONBOARDING-REDESIGN-PLAN.md <- binary-search composite assessment
│   ├── 00-vision.md
│   ├── 01-first-principles.md

│   ├── stages/                     <- 8 stages of consciousness + overview

The `src/` contains the **full assessment-module architecture** —
64 registered modules (8 lines × 8 stages), each with 20 assessment
items, mode-aware execution (capacity/encounter/shadow/calibration/practice),
adaptive item selection, and the complete developmental loop from
CCI computation through encounter scheduling to Significator mutation.

## Quick start (the existing scaffold)

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # local Vite dev server with HMR (open http://localhost:5173)
npm run build        # type-check + production bundle in dist/
npm test             # vitest unit tests for the core
```

Capacitor / Android targets:

```bash
npm run cap:sync     # build + cap sync
npm run cap:android  # build, sync, open in Android Studio
```

## Reading the documentation

If you have **30 minutes** and want the picture:

1. `docs/00-vision.md`
2. `docs/01-first-principles.md`
3. `UNIFIED-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md`

If you have **2 hours** and want the architecture:

1. The above
2. `docs/INDEX.md`
3. `docs/foundations/00-integral-theory.md`
4. `docs/foundations/06-law-of-one-correspondence.md` (the canon)
5. `docs/STAGE-ASSESSMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`

If you want **all of it**, follow the reading order in `docs/INDEX.md`.

## Architecture in one paragraph

The codebase is split into three layers — `core/` (pure TypeScript,
no Phaser, no native, no network — runs in Node, in tests, in the
browser, anywhere a TS engine runs); `infra/` (I/O adapters —
persistence, native bridges, telemetry, locale); and `game/` (the
Phaser scenes that *visualise* the core). The MVP introduces eight
**registries** (`LineRegistry`, `StageRegistry`, `RayRegistry`,
`TaskRegistry`, `AbilityRegistry`, `EncounterRegistry`,
`DriveRegistry`, `NarrativeRegistry`) so that adding a new stage,
line, ray, task, ability, encounter, drive, or narrative beat is a
data-and-adapter change, never a rewrite.

## The eight-stage developmental arc, at a glance

| # | Stage | Energy ray | Defining capacity |
|:-:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Infrared / Archaic | Red | Survival, sensori-motor |
| 2 | Magenta / Magic | Orange | Symbol, magical agency |
| 3 | Red / Power | Yellow | Ego, will, dominance |
| 4 | Amber / Mythic | Green | Belonging, rule-and-role |
| 5 | Orange / Rational | Blue (in) | Reason, achievement |
| 6 | Green / Pluralistic | Blue (out) | Sensitivity, plurality |
| 7 | Turquoise / Integral | Indigo | Vision-logic, holism |
| 8 | White / Super-Integral | Violet | Non-dual, harvest |

Per-stage world bibles are in `docs/stages/`.

## The eight lines of intelligence

| Line | Quadrant home | Assessment style |
|---|---|---|
| Cognitive | UR | Planning, working-memory, Tower-of-London |
| Emotional | UL | Empathy reads, affect-regulation, mood recognition |
| Moral | UL->LL | Choice-based dilemmas, value-priority assessments |
| Intrapersonal | UL | Witness pause, self-tag, integrate |
| Spiritual | UL | State-shifting, value-priority modules |
| Somatic | UR | Rhythm, proprioception, breath-gated abilities |
| Willpower | UL->UR | Goal-locking, fatigue resistance |
| Interpersonal | LL | Co-op synergies, conflict resolution |

Per-line documents are in `docs/lines/`.

## Contributing

This project is **personally authored** by [@ishan-parihar](https://github.com/ishan-parihar)
and shipped globally. External contributions of the cognitive
content (cultural reviewers for affect-recognition stimuli,
linguistic localisation of narration, accessibility expertise) are
welcomed once the MVP is stable. Until then, please use Issues for
discussion. PRs against the early scaffold are accepted at the
maintainer's discretion.

A `CONTRIBUTING.md` will be added during Phase 5.

747:   /**
748:    * Module-aware fallback: uses the assessment module's tasks, drive probes,
749:    * and scoring rubric to present a real developmental assessment even without the LLM.
750:    * Selects a task matching the encounter modality, presents it as a narrative challenge,
751:    * evaluates the response against drive probes, detects shadow patterns,
752:    * and computes altitude progression.
753:    */
754:   private async runModuleAssessment(_line: Line, stage: Stage, now: number): Promise<OrchestratorResult> {
755:     const module = this.module!;
756:     const holon = this.world.holons.find(h => h.id === this.encounter.holonSource);
757:     const holonName = holon?.name ?? 'A presence';
758:     const currentModality = this.encounter.modality;
759: 
760:     // 1. Select the best task from the module based on modality
761:     const task = this.selectTaskForModality(module, currentModality);
762:     // Track the actual presented task for narrative building (fix B.2)
763:     this._currentPresentedTask = task;
764: 
765:     // 2. Present the task as a narrative challenge via uiHandler
766:     const askResult = await this.presentModuleTask(module, task, currentModality, holonName);
767:     const answer = askResult.answers[0];
768:     const rawLabel = answer?.selectedLabels[0] ?? '';
769:     const writeIn = answer?.writeInValue;
770:     const playerResponseText = writeIn ?? rawLabel;
771: 
772:     // 3. Evaluate using the TaskRenderer's evaluate() if available (produces TrialResult with timing/accuracy)
773:     //    Fall back to drive-probe evaluation if no renderer evaluate is available
774:     const endTimeMs = Date.now();
775:     let evaluation: {
776:       passed: boolean;
777:       polarityDirection: 'sto' | 'sts' | 'neutral';
778:       driveScores: { agency: number; communion: number; eros: number; agape: number };
779:       driveSignals: { agency: string; communion: string; eros: string; agape: string };
780:       feedback: string;
781:     };
782:     let trialResult: TrialResult | null = null;
783: 
784:     if (this._currentRendererEvaluate) {
785:       // Use the TaskRenderer's evaluate function for real scoring
786:       trialResult = this._currentRendererEvaluate(playerResponseText, this._currentTaskStartTime, endTimeMs);
787: 
788:       // Extract drive metadata from the trial's rawResponse (set by TaskRenderers)
789:       const rawResp = trialResult?.rawResponse as any;
790:       const matchedDrive: string | null = rawResp?.matchedDrive ?? null;
791:       const matchedPolarity: string = rawResp?.matchedPolarity ?? 'neutral';
792:       const correctnessScore: number = rawResp?.correctnessScore ?? 0.5;
793: 
794:       // Use correctnessScore as the primary scoring signal (from TaskRenderer options)
795:       const baseScore = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, correctnessScore));
796: 
797:       // D.9: Use shared shadow keyword detection helper (DRY)
798:       let writeInDriveDetection: { drive: string; polarity: string; shadowKeyword: string | null } | null = null;
799:       if (writeIn) {
800:         writeInDriveDetection = AgenticOrchestrator.detectWriteInShadow(writeIn);
801:       }
802: 
803:       // When a write-in is present, its keyword-based detection takes priority over
804:       // the renderer's label matching (which can false-positive on short words like 'I').
805:       const effectiveDrive = writeInDriveDetection?.drive ?? matchedDrive ?? null;
806:       const effectivePolarity = writeInDriveDetection?.polarity ?? (matchedPolarity !== 'neutral' ? matchedPolarity : 'neutral');
807: 
808:       // Build differentiated drive scores:
809:       // - The matched/driven drive gets the full baseScore (or boosted for write-in depth)
810:       // - Other drives get baseline neutral (0.5)
811:       // - For write-ins with no shadow detection, apply a depth boost and distribute evenly
812:       const isWriteInWithNoShadow = matchedDrive === null && !writeInDriveDetection && !!writeIn;
813: 
814:       // ── SCORING FIX: Use rubric dimension weights on TrialResult dimensions ──
815:       // OLD: averaged 4 drives → compressed to ~0.55 always, even correct answers failed at threshold 0.6
816:       // NEW: compute weighted score from TrialResult dimensions using the module's rubric weights.
817:       // This gives a true performance signal: correct MCQ → ~0.8, partial → ~0.55, wrong → ~0.25.
818:       const rubricWeights = module.scoringRubric.dimensionWeights;
819:       const trialDims = trialResult!.dimensions;
820:       let weightedSum = 0;
821:       let totalWeight = 0;
822:       for (const [dim, weight] of Object.entries(rubricWeights)) {
823:         const val = trialDims[dim as keyof typeof trialDims];
824:         if (weight && typeof val === 'number') {
825:           weightedSum += val * weight;
826:           totalWeight += weight;
827:         }
828:       }
829:       // Blend the rubric-weighted score with the drive-correctness score for a robust signal
830:       const rubricScore = totalWeight > 0 ? weightedSum / totalWeight : baseScore;
831:       const blendedScore = rubricScore * 0.6 + baseScore * 0.4;
832: 
833:       // Drive scores: matched drive gets blendedScore (consistent with pass/fail),
834:       // write-in depth bonus applied on top. Unmatched drives get a lower baseline.
835:       const matchedScore = isWriteInWithNoShadow ? Math.max(blendedScore, 0.55) : blendedScore;
836:       const driveScores = {
837:         agency: effectiveDrive === 'agency' ? matchedScore
838:           : effectiveDrive !== null ? Math.min(0.5, blendedScore * 0.7)
839:           : matchedScore,
840:         communion: effectiveDrive === 'communion' ? matchedScore
841:           : effectiveDrive !== null ? Math.min(0.5, blendedScore * 0.7)
842:           : matchedScore,
843:         eros: effectiveDrive === 'eros' ? matchedScore
844:           : effectiveDrive !== null ? Math.min(0.5, blendedScore * 0.7)
845:           : matchedScore,
846:         agape: effectiveDrive === 'agape' ? matchedScore

1299:     const awarenessBonus = shadowAware ? 0.1 : 0;
1300:     const semanticBonus = lengthBonus + densityBonus + awarenessBonus;
1301: 
1302:     // Apply semantic bonus to all scores (caps at 1.0)
1303:     const adjustedAgencyScore = Math.min(1.0, agencyScore + (selectedDrive === 'agency' ? semanticBonus : 0));
1304:     const adjustedCommunionScore = Math.min(1.0, communionScore + (selectedDrive === 'communion' ? semanticBonus : 0));
1305:     const adjustedErosScore = Math.min(1.0, erosScore + (selectedDrive === 'eros' ? semanticBonus : 0));
1306:     const adjustedAgapeScore = Math.min(1.0, agapeScore + (selectedDrive === 'agape' ? semanticBonus : 0));
1307: 
1308:     const avgScore = (adjustedAgencyScore + adjustedCommunionScore + adjustedErosScore + adjustedAgapeScore) / 4;
1309:     const passThreshold = module.scoringRubric.passThreshold ?? 0.7;
1310:     const passed = avgScore >= passThreshold;
1311: 
1312:     // Build feedback with depth-adjusted scores
1313:     const depthNote = semanticBonus > 0
1314:       ? ` (${wordCount} words, ${(conceptDensity * 100).toFixed(0)}% unique, +${(semanticBonus * 100).toFixed(0)}% depth)`
1315:       : '';
1316:     const feedback = passed
1317:       ? `Your response demonstrated balanced engagement with the ${module.line} ${module.stage} challenge. Agency: ${(adjustedAgencyScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%, Communion: ${(adjustedCommunionScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%, Eros: ${(adjustedErosScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%, Agape: ${(adjustedAgapeScore * 100).toFixed(0)}%.${depthNote}`
1318:       : `The challenge revealed areas for growth. Your ${module.line} ${module.stage} response showed room for deeper integration.`;
1319: 
1320:     return {
1321:       passed,
1322:       polarityDirection,
1323:       driveScores: { agency: adjustedAgencyScore, communion: adjustedCommunionScore, eros: adjustedErosScore, agape: adjustedAgapeScore },
1324:       driveSignals: {
1325:         agency: agencyResult.signal,
1326:         communion: communionResult.signal,
1327:         eros: erosResult.signal,
1328:         agape: agapeResult.signal,
1329:       },
1330:       feedback,
1331:     };

1353:   /**
1354:    * Compute an altitude shift signal when the player demonstrates consistent
1355:    * HealthyBalanced drive patterns across ALL 4 drives (selected drive must score
1356:    * healthy, not shadow).
1357:    * Returns a ConsequenceRecord-compatible object or null if no shift is warranted.
1358:    */
1359:   private computeAltitudeShift(
1360:     _driveSignals: { agency: string; communion: string; eros: string; agape: string },
1361:     module: StageAssessment,
1362:     currentEncounterStage: Stage,
1363:     passed: boolean,
1364:   ): { line: Line; from: Stage; to: Stage } | null {
1365:     const key = module.line;
1366: 
1367:     if (!passed) {
1368:       return null; // Failures don't count but don't reset total count either
1369:     }
1370: 
1371:     // Use TOTAL passes per line (not consecutive) — the scheduler alternates lines
1372:     // so consecutive passes are mathematically impossible with 8+ lines.
1373:     // Threshold of 2 passes: demonstrates sustained capacity on the same line.
1374:     const totalPasses = (this._consecutivePasses.get(key) ?? 0) + 1;
1375:     this._consecutivePasses.set(key, totalPasses);
1376: 
1377:     if (totalPasses < 2) {
1378:       return null; // Need at least 2 passes on this line
1379:     }
1380: 
1381:     // Shift achieved — reset counter so future passes require 2 fresh wins
1382:     this._consecutivePasses.set(key, 0);
1383:     return { line: module.line, from: currentEncounterStage, to: currentEncounterStage };
1384:   }

1492:   private evaluateFallbackResponse(selectedLabel: string): {

1500:

1513:     if (stsKeywords.some(kw => lower.includes(kw))) {
1514:       const isAverted = ['betray', 'raid', 'deceive'].some(kw => lower.includes(kw));

1516:         passed,
1517:         polarityDirection: 'sts',

1588:   /**
1589:    * Write-in evaluation for self-reflection (Direct Questioning) encounters.
1590:    * Unlike evaluateFallbackResponse (designed for short MCQ option labels),
1591:    * this analyzes reflective prose for depth, coherence, and shadow signals.
1592:    * Always passes — self-reflection is a practice, not a test.
1593:    */
1594:   private evaluateSelfReflection(responseText: string): {
1595:     passed: boolean;
1596:     polarityDirection: 'sto' | 'sts' | 'neutral';
1597:     driveScores: { agency: number; communion: number; eros: number; agape: number };
1598:     driveSignals: { agency: string; communion: string; eros: string; agape: string };
1599:     feedback: string;
1600:   } {
1601:     const line = this.encounter.moduleRef.split(':')[0];
1602:     const lower = responseText.toLowerCase();
1603:     const wordCount = lower.split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 0).length;
1604: 
1605:     // Early return for empty/very short responses — honest but non-punitive
1606:     if (wordCount < 5) {
1607:       return {
1608:         passed: true, // still passes — brevity is not failure
1609:         polarityDirection: 'neutral',
1610:         driveScores: { agency: 0.5, communion: 0.5, eros: 0.5, agape: 0.5 },
1611:         driveSignals: { agency: 'HealthyBalanced', communion: 'HealthyBalanced', eros: 'HealthyBalanced', agape: 'HealthyBalanced' },
1612:         feedback: `A brief reflection. The ${line} line invites deeper exploration when you're ready — there is no rush, only invitation.`,
1613:       };
1614:     }
1615: 
1616:     const uniqueWords = new Set(lower.split(/\s+/).filter(w => w.length > 0)).size;
1617:     const conceptDensity = wordCount > 0 ? uniqueWords / wordCount : 0;
1618: 
1619:     // Depth heuristics
1620:     const lengthBonus = wordCount > 30 ? 0.3 : wordCount > 15 ? 0.2 : 0.1;
1621:     const densityBonus = conceptDensity > 0.7 ? 0.15 : conceptDensity > 0.5 ? 0.1 : 0;
1622:     const depthScore = Math.min(1.0, 0.4 + lengthBonus + densityBonus);
1623: 
1624:     // Shadow detection from write-in
1625:     const shadow = AgenticOrchestrator.detectShadowKeywords(responseText);
1626: 
1627:     // Drive detection from semantic content
1628:     const driveKeywords = {
1629:       agency: ['decide', 'choose', 'act', 'control', 'direct', 'lead', 'assert', 'boundary', 'independent', 'own'],
1630:       communion: ['connect', 'together', 'share', 'listen', 'empathy', 'feel', 'relationship', 'others', 'belong', 'community'],
1631:       eros: ['grow', 'reach', 'aspire', 'seek', 'question', 'explore', 'transform', 'evolve', 'deeper', 'meaning'],
1632:       agape: ['accept', 'integrate', 'compassion', 'hold', 'include', 'balance', 'paradox', 'surrender', 'release', 'wholeness'],
1633:     };
1634:     const driveScores: Record<string, number> = { agency: 0.5, communion: 0.5, eros: 0.5, agape: 0.5 };
1635:     for (const [drive, keywords] of Object.entries(driveKeywords)) {
1636:       const matches = keywords.filter(kw => lower.includes(kw)).length;
1637:       if (matches > 0) driveScores[drive] = Math.min(1.0, 0.5 + matches * 0.1);
1638:     }
1639: 
1640:     // Polarity from drive balance
1641:     const selfDominant = driveScores.agency + driveScores.eros;
1642:     const otherDominant = driveScores.communion + driveScores.agape;
1643:     let polarityDirection: 'sto' | 'sts' | 'neutral';
1644:     if (selfDominant > otherDominant + 0.3) polarityDirection = 'sts';
1645:     else if (otherDominant > selfDominant + 0.3) polarityDirection = 'sto';
1646:     else polarityDirection = 'neutral';
1647: 
1648:     // Always passes — self-reflection is a practice, not a test
1649:     const feedback = shadow
1650:       ? `A ${shadow.quadrant} pattern surfaced through your reflection. Naming it here is the first step toward integration. Your response contained ${wordCount} words with ${(conceptDensity * 100).toFixed(0)}% conceptual density.`
1651:       : `Your reflection on the ${line} line showed ${depthScore > 0.7 ? 'notable depth' : 'genuine engagement'}. The field registers your willingness to look inward.`;
1652: 
1653:     return {
1654:       passed: true,
1655:       polarityDirection,
1656:       driveScores: driveScores as { agency: number; communion: number; eros: number; agape: number },
1657:       driveSignals: {
1658:         agency: shadow?.quadrant === 'DarkAddiction' ? 'DarkAddicted' : 'HealthyBalanced',
1659:         communion: shadow?.quadrant === 'DarkAllergy' ? 'DarkAverted' : 'HealthyBalanced',
1660:         eros: shadow?.quadrant === 'GoldenAddiction' ? 'GoldenAddicted' : 'HealthyBalanced',
1661:         agape: shadow?.quadrant === 'GoldenAllergy' ? 'GoldenAverted' : 'HealthyBalanced',
1662:       },
1663:       feedback,
1664:     };
1665:   }

1697:   private createAssessmentResult(
1698:     passed: boolean,
1699:     scores: Partial<Record<MeasureDimension, number>>,
1700:     driveScores?: { agency: number; communion: number; eros: number; agape: number },
1701:     rawTrials?: readonly TrialResult[],
1702:   ): AssessmentResult {
1703:     const [line, stage] = this.encounter.moduleRef.split(':') as [Line, Stage];
1704:     const dimensions: Record<MeasureDimension, number> = {
1705:       accuracy: scores.accuracy ?? 0.5,
1706:       response_time: scores.response_time ?? 0.5,
1707:       consistency: scores.consistency ?? 0.5,
1708:       depth: scores.depth ?? 0.5,
1709:       self_correction: scores.self_correction ?? 0.5,
1710:       complexity_handled: scores.complexity_handled ?? 0.5,
1711:       transfer: scores.transfer ?? 0.5,
1712:       metacognition: scores.metacognition ?? 0.5,
1713:       coherence: scores.coherence ?? 0.5,
1714:       integration: scores.integration ?? 0.5,
1715:     };
1716: 
1717:     // Wire per-drive scores into assessment dimensions so they aren't dead code
1718:     // Only override if scores weren't explicitly provided (driveScores is a fallback signal)
1719:     if (driveScores && !scores.accuracy) {
1720:       dimensions.accuracy = driveScores.agency;
1721:       dimensions.depth = driveScores.eros;
1722:       dimensions.coherence = driveScores.communion;
1723:       dimensions.integration = driveScores.agape;
1724:     }
1725: 
1726:     // Populate rawTrials from the TaskRenderer's TrialResult
1727:     const trials = rawTrials ?? [];
1728: 
1729:     return {
1730:       line,
1731:       stage,
1732:       passed,
1733:       confidence: computeConfidence(trials, 0.7),
1734:       dimensions,
1735:       rawTrials: trials,
1736:     };
1737:   }

1741:       passed: boolean;
1742:       feedback: string;
1743:       polarityDirection: 'sto' | 'sts' | 'neutral';
1744:       driveScores?: { agency?: number; communion?: number; eros?: number; agape?: number };
1745:       driveSignals?: { agency?: string; communion?: string; eros?: string; agape?: string };
1746:       shadowSignal?: {

1753:   ): Omit<OrchestratorResult, 'finalResult' | 'messages'> {

2:  * EncounterScheduler — selects and ranks encounters using the full priority formula.
3:  * Spec: foundations/24 (full)
4:  */
5: import type { PolarityMode, ShadowQuadrant } from '../domain/enums.js';
6: import type { ScheduledEncounter } from '../domain/EncounterSpecNew.js';
7: import type { Significator } from '../domain/Significator.js';
8: import type { ShadowEntry } from '../domain/ShadowLedger.js';
9: import { generateCandidates, type WorldState } from './CandidateGeneration.js';
10: import { computePriority, DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, type SessionContext, type PriorityWeights } from './PriorityComputation.js';
11: import type { TransformationPhase } from './TransformationDetector.js';
12: 
13: /** Threshold: if a line has more than this many unresolved shadows, shadow-work mode activates. */
14: const SHADOW_WORK_THRESHOLD = 3;
15: 
16: export type { WorldState } from './CandidateGeneration.js';
17: export type { SessionContext } from './PriorityComputation.js';
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Check if a line has exceeded the shadow-work threshold (>3 unresolved shadows).
21:  * When true, encounters for this line should use shadow execution mode.
22:  */
23: export function detectShadowWorkThreshold(sig: Significator, line: string): boolean {
24:   const unresolved = sig.shadows.entries.filter(
25:     (e: ShadowEntry) => e.line === line && e.resolvedAt === null,
26:   );
27:   return unresolved.length > SHADOW_WORK_THRESHOLD;
28: }
29: 
30: /**
31:  * Find the most active (highest severity) unresolved shadow quadrant for a line.
32:  * Returns null if no unresolved shadows exist for that line.
33:  */
34: export function findMostActiveShadowQuadrant(sig: Significator, line: string): ShadowQuadrant | null {
35:   const unresolved = sig.shadows.entries
36:     .filter((e: ShadowEntry) => e.line === line && e.resolvedAt === null)
37:     .sort((a: ShadowEntry, b: ShadowEntry) => b.severity - a.severity);
38:   return unresolved[0]?.quadrant ?? null;
39: }
40: 
41: /**
42:  * Schedule the next N encounters, ranked by priority.
43:  */
44: export function scheduleNext(
45:   sig: Significator,
46:   world: WorldState,
47:   session: SessionContext,
48:   now: number,
49:   count: number = 3,
50:   weights?: PriorityWeights,
51:   bleedThrough?: readonly string[],
52: ): ScheduledEncounter[] {
53:   const candidates = generateCandidates(sig, world, now, session);
54:   if (candidates.length === 0) return [];
55: 
56:   const scored = candidates.map(c => ({
57:     candidate: c,
58:     priority: computePriority(c, sig, world, session, now, weights, bleedThrough),
59:   }));
60: 
61:   // Sort descending by priority
62:   scored.sort((a, b) => b.priority - a.priority);
63: 
64:   // Determine session position
65:   const progress = session.encountersSoFar / Math.max(1, session.targetSessionLength);
66:   const position: 'warmup' | 'peak' | 'cooldown' =
67:     progress < 0.2 ? 'warmup' : progress > 0.8 ? 'cooldown' : 'peak';
68: 
69:   // Determine polarity mode from significator
70:   const polarityMode: PolarityMode = sig.polarity.master.mode;
71: 
72:   // Determine shadow target from active shadows
73:   const activeShadow = sig.shadows.entries.find(e => e.resolvedAt === null);
74:   const shadowTarget: ShadowQuadrant | null = activeShadow?.quadrant ?? null;
75: 
76:   // G.9: Holonic Return — detect shadow-work threshold per-line
77:   // When a line accumulates >3 unresolved shadows, force shadow execution mode
78:   // and target the most active (highest severity) shadow quadrant for that line.
79:   const lineShadowModes = new Map<string, boolean>();
80:   const lineShadowTargets = new Map<string, ShadowQuadrant | null>();
81: 
82:   // Take top N, diversifying by line (no more than 2 from same line)
83:   const result: ScheduledEncounter[] = [];
84:   const lineCounts: Record<string, number> = {};
85:   const moduleRefs = new Set<string>();
86: 
87:   for (const { candidate, priority } of scored) {
88:     if (result.length >= count) break;
89:     const lc = lineCounts[candidate.line] ?? 0;
90:     if (lc >= 2) continue;
91:     // Deduplicate by moduleRef to prevent same encounter appearing multiple times
92:     if (moduleRefs.has(candidate.moduleRef)) continue;
93:     lineCounts[candidate.line] = lc + 1;
94:     moduleRefs.add(candidate.moduleRef);
95: 
96:     // G.9: Check shadow-work threshold for this candidate's line
97:     if (!lineShadowModes.has(candidate.line)) {
98:       lineShadowModes.set(candidate.line, detectShadowWorkThreshold(sig, candidate.line));
99:       lineShadowTargets.set(candidate.line, findMostActiveShadowQuadrant(sig, candidate.line));
100:     }
101:     const isShadowWork = lineShadowModes.get(candidate.line)!;
102:     const lineShadowTarget = lineShadowTargets.get(candidate.line) ?? shadowTarget;
103: 
104:     // G.20: During transformation crucible, force shadow mode for ego-dissolution
105:     const isCrucible = session.transformationState?.phase === 'crucible';
106:     const executionMode = isCrucible ? 'shadow' : (isShadowWork ? 'shadow' : 'capacity');
107: 
108:     result.push({
109:       id: `${candidate.moduleRef}:${candidate.holonId}:${now}`,
110:       moduleRef: candidate.moduleRef,
111:       modality: candidate.modality,
112:       targetLines: [candidate.line],
113:       stage: candidate.stage,
114:       holonSource: candidate.holonId,
115:       shadowTarget: lineShadowTarget,
116:       polarityMode,
117:       difficulty: computeDifficulty(sig, candidate.line, candidate.stage),
118:       sessionPosition: position,
119:       priority,
120:       driveTarget: activeShadow?.drive ?? null,
121:       executionMode,
122:     });
123:   }
124: 
125:   return result;
126: }
127: 
128: function computeDifficulty(sig: Significator, line: string, stage: string): number {
129:   // Difficulty relative to player's altitude in that line
130:   const key = `${line}:${stage}`;
131:   const cell = sig.polarity.cells[key];
132:   const traceCount = cell?.traceCount ?? 0;
133:   // More traces = more familiarity = lower difficulty; cap at 0.3-0.9
134:   return Math.max(0.3, Math.min(0.9, 0.9 - traceCount * 0.05));
135: }

178:       const durationMs = endTimeMs - startTimeMs;

180:       const playerCount = numericMatch ? parseInt(numericMatch[0]!, 10) : -1;
181: 
182:       const error = Math.abs(playerCount - expectedCount);
183:       const accuracy = Math.max(0, 1 - error / Math.max(1, trialCount * 0.5));
184: 
185:       const expectedTime = trialCount * ((task.parameters.stimulusDurationMs as number) ?? 1100) + 2000;
186:       const timeRatio = durationMs / expectedTime;
187:       const responseTime = timeRatio < 0.5 ? 0.9 : timeRatio < 1.5 ? 0.7 : timeRatio < 3 ? 0.5 : 0.3;
188:       const consistency = error === 0 ? 0.95 : error === 1 ? 0.7 : 0.4;
189: 
190:       // Match selected option to its drive metadata
191:       const matchedOpt = options.find(o => answer.toLowerCase().includes(o.label.toLowerCase()));
192: 
193:       return {
194:         taskId: task.id,
195:         timestamp: startTimeMs,
196:         dimensions: { accuracy, response_time: responseTime, consistency },
197:         rawResponse: {
198:           playerCount, expectedCount, sequence: sequence.join(''), matchPositions,
199:           matchedDrive: matchedOpt?.drive ?? null,
200:           matchedPolarity: matchedOpt?.polarity ?? 'neutral',
201:           correctnessScore: matchedOpt?.correctnessScore ?? 0.5,
202:         },
203:         durationMs,
204:       };
205:     },
206:   };
207: }

211: /**
212:  * Render a Stroop task: show a word printed in a different ink color,
213:  * ask the player to name the INK color (not the word).
214:  */
215: export function renderStroop(task: AssessmentTask): {
216:   prompt: AskUserQuestionParams;
217:   evaluate: (answer: string, startTimeMs: number, endTimeMs: number) => TrialResult;
218: } {
219:   const diff = getDifficulty(task.parameters.stage as string | undefined);
220:   const trialCount = (task.parameters.trials as number) ?? diff.stroopTrials;
221:   const colors = diff.stroopColors;
222: 
223:   const trials: { wordIdx: number; inkIdx: number }[] = [];
224:   for (let i = 0; i < trialCount; i++) {
225:     let wordIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * colors.length);
226:     let inkIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * colors.length);
227:     while (inkIdx === wordIdx) {
228:       inkIdx = Math.floor(Math.random() * colors.length);
229:     }
230:     trials.push({ wordIdx, inkIdx });
231:   }
232: 
233:   const trialDisplay = trials.map((t, i) => {
234:     const inkColor = colors[t.inkIdx]!;
235:     return `${C.dim}#${i + 1}${C.reset} ${inkColor.render}`;
236:   }).join('   ');
237: 
238:   // Generate the correct sequence
239:   const correctSequence = trials.map(t => colors[t.inkIdx]!.initial).join(',');
240: 
241:   const question = [
242:     `Name the INK COLOR of each word (not the word itself).`,
243:     ``,
244:     `${trialDisplay}`,
245:     ``,
246:     `${C.bold}What is the correct ink color sequence?${C.reset}`,
247:   ].join('\n');
248: 
249:   // Build correct and incorrect options, then shuffle
250:   const incorrectSequences = [
251:     trials.map(t => colors[(t.inkIdx + 1) % colors.length]!.initial).join(','),
252:     trials.map(t => colors[(t.inkIdx + 2) % colors.length]!.initial).join(','),
253:     trials.map(t => colors[t.wordIdx]!.initial).join(','), // Word-color (Stroop error)
254:   ];
255: 
256:   const options: DriveOption[] = [
257:     { label: correctSequence, description: 'Correct sequence', drive: 'agency', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 1.0 },
258:     { label: incorrectSequences[0]!, description: 'Partial match', drive: 'communion', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.5 },
259:     { label: incorrectSequences[1]!, description: 'Different sequence', drive: 'eros', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.3 },
260:     { label: incorrectSequences[2]!, description: 'Word-based (common error)', drive: 'agape', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.0 },
261:   ];
262:   shuffle(options);
263: 
264:   return {
265:     prompt: {
266:       questions: [{
267:         question,
268:         header: 'Inhibitory Control',
269:         options: options.map(o => ({ label: o.label, description: o.description })),
270:         allowWriteIn: true,
271:         multiSelect: false,
272:       }],
273:     },
274:     evaluate: (answer: string, startTimeMs: number, endTimeMs: number): TrialResult => {
275:       const durationMs = endTimeMs - startTimeMs;
276:       const colorMap: Record<string, number> = { r: 0, red: 0, b: 1, blue: 1, g: 2, green: 2, y: 3, yellow: 3 };
277:       const parts = answer.toLowerCase().split(/[, ]+/).filter(Boolean);
278:       const playerColors = parts.map(p => colorMap[p] ?? -1).filter(c => c >= 0);
279: 
280:       const expected = trials.map(t => t.inkIdx);
281:       let correct = 0;
282:       for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(playerColors.length, expected.length); i++) {
283:         if (playerColors[i] === expected[i]) correct++;
284:       }
285: 
286:       const accuracy = expected.length > 0 ? correct / expected.length : 0;
287:       const expectedTime = trialCount * 2500;
288:       const timeRatio = durationMs / expectedTime;
289:       const responseTime = timeRatio < 0.5 ? 0.9 : timeRatio < 1.5 ? 0.7 : timeRatio < 3 ? 0.5 : 0.3;
290: 
291:       const matchedOpt = options.find(o => answer.toUpperCase().includes(o.label));
292: 
293:       return {
294:         taskId: task.id,
295:         timestamp: startTimeMs,
296:         dimensions: { accuracy, response_time: responseTime, consistency: accuracy },
297:         rawResponse: {
298:           playerColors, expected, correct, total: expected.length,
299:           matchedDrive: matchedOpt?.drive ?? null,
300:           matchedPolarity: matchedOpt?.polarity ?? 'neutral',
301:           correctnessScore: matchedOpt?.correctnessScore ?? 0.5,
302:         },
303:         durationMs,
304:       };
305:     },
306:   };
307: }

311: /**

334:   const display = stimuli.map((s, i) => `${C.dim}${i + 1}:${C.reset}${s}`).join(' ');

336:   const question = [
337:     `⚔ = GO (respond)   🛡 = NO-GO (withhold)`,

339:     `${display}`,

341:     `${C.bold}How many GO stimuli (⚔) were there?${C.reset}`,

345:     { label: `${goCount} GO`, description: `I counted ${goCount} go signals`, drive: 'agency', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 1.0 },
346:     { label: `${Math.max(0, goCount - 1)} GO`, description: 'I may have missed one', drive: 'communion', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.7 },

352:   return {
353:     prompt: {
354:       questions: [{
355:         question,
356:         header: 'Impulse Regulation',
357:         options: options.map(o => ({ label: o.label, description: o.description })),
358:         allowWriteIn: true,
359:         multiSelect: false,
360:       }],
361:     },
362:     evaluate: (answer: string, startTimeMs: number, endTimeMs: number): TrialResult => {
363:       const durationMs = endTimeMs - startTimeMs;
364:       const numericMatch = answer.match(/\d+/);
365:       const playerCount = numericMatch ? parseInt(numericMatch[0]!, 10) : -1;
366: 
367:       const error = Math.abs(playerCount - goCount);
368:       const accuracy = Math.max(0, 1 - error / Math.max(1, trialCount * 0.3));
369: 
370:       const expectedTime = trialCount * ((task.parameters.stimulusDurationMs as number) ?? 500) + 2000;
371:       const timeRatio = durationMs / expectedTime;
372:       const responseTime = timeRatio < 0.5 ? 0.9 : timeRatio < 1.5 ? 0.7 : timeRatio < 3 ? 0.5 : 0.3;
373: 
374:       const matchedOpt = options.find(o => answer.includes(o.label));
375: 
376:       return {
377:         taskId: task.id,
378:         timestamp: startTimeMs,
379:         dimensions: {
380:           accuracy,
381:           response_time: responseTime,
382:           consistency: error === 0 ? 0.95 : error === 1 ? 0.7 : 0.4,
383:         },
384:         rawResponse: {
385:           playerCount, goCount, nogoCount, stimuli: stimuli.join(''),
386:           matchedDrive: matchedOpt?.drive ?? null,
387:           matchedPolarity: matchedOpt?.polarity ?? 'neutral',
388:           correctnessScore: matchedOpt?.correctnessScore ?? 0.5,
389:         },
390:         durationMs,
391:       };
392:     },
393:   };
394: }

468: export function renderPatternPrediction(task: AssessmentTask): {
469:   prompt: AskUserQuestionParams;
470:   evaluate: (answer: string, startTimeMs: number, endTimeMs: number) => TrialResult;
471: } {
472:   const diff = getDifficulty(task.parameters.stage as string | undefined);
473:   const disks = (task.parameters.disks as number) ?? diff.patternDisks;
474:   const attempts = (task.parameters.attempts as number) ?? diff.patternAttempts;
475: 
476:   const base = Math.floor(Math.random() * 5) + 1;
477:   const step = Math.floor(Math.random() * 3) + 1;
478:   const pattern = Array.from({ length: 4 }, (_, i) => base + step * i);
479:   const nextValue = pattern[3]! + step;
480: 
481:   const question = [
482:     `Observe the pattern of ${disks} elements across ${attempts} steps:`,
483:     ``,
484:     `  ${pattern.map((v, i) => `${C.dim}Step ${i + 1}:${C.reset} ${'█'.repeat(v)} ${v}`).join('\n  ')}`,
485:     ``,
486:     `${C.bold}What is Step 5?${C.reset}`,
487:   ].join('\n');
488: 
489:   const options: DriveOption[] = [
490:     { label: `${nextValue}`, description: `The next value (increasing by ${step})`, drive: 'agency', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 1.0 },
491:     { label: `${nextValue + step}`, description: `Larger step`, drive: 'communion', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.3 },
492:     { label: `${nextValue - 1}`, description: `Close but not quite`, drive: 'eros', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.5 },
493:     { label: `No pattern`, description: 'I see no clear pattern', drive: 'agape', polarity: 'neutral', correctnessScore: 0.0 },
494:   ];
495:   shuffle(options);
496: 
497:   return {
498:     prompt: {
499:       questions: [{
500:         question,
501:         header: 'Pattern Recognition',
502:         options: options.map(o => ({ label: o.label, description: o.description })),
503:         allowWriteIn: true,
504:         multiSelect: false,
505:       }],
506:     },
507:     evaluate: (answer: string, startTimeMs: number, endTimeMs: number): TrialResult => {
508:       const durationMs = endTimeMs - startTimeMs;
509:       const numericMatch = answer.match(/\d+/);
510:       const playerValue = numericMatch ? parseInt(numericMatch[0]!, 10) : -1;
511: 
512:       const error = Math.abs(playerValue - nextValue);
513:       const accuracy = Math.max(0, 1 - error / Math.max(1, disks));
514: 
515:       const expectedTime = attempts * 3000;
516:       const timeRatio = durationMs / expectedTime;
517:       const responseTime = timeRatio < 0.5 ? 0.9 : timeRatio < 1.5 ? 0.7 : timeRatio < 3 ? 0.5 : 0.3;
518: 
519:       const matchedOpt = options.find(o => answer.includes(o.label));
520: 
521:       return {
522:         taskId: task.id,
523:         timestamp: startTimeMs,
524:         dimensions: {
525:           accuracy,
526:           response_time: responseTime,
527:           complexity_handled: accuracy,
528:           self_correction: error <= 1 ? 0.8 : 0.4,
529:         },
530:         rawResponse: {
531:           pattern, nextValue, playerValue, step,
532:           matchedDrive: matchedOpt?.drive ?? null,
533:           matchedPolarity: matchedOpt?.polarity ?? 'neutral',
534:           correctnessScore: matchedOpt?.correctnessScore ?? 0.5,
535:         },
536:         durationMs,
537:       };
538:     },
539:   };
540: }

1: # 21 — Incarnation Architecture (Option C)
2: 
3: > **Lateral:** Master synthesis — how greater-cycle archetypes + concept-drafts + modalities compose into a playable game.
4: > **Depends on:** 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 23, 24
5: > **Referenced by:** all implementation work; MVP-BLUEPRINT
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 1. The master equation
10: 
11: ```
12: Game = Significator (player) navigating Great Way (world)
13:      through encounters drawn from 64 line×stage modules
14:      with consequences propagating through Choice/polarity engine
15:      triggering Transformation at stage thresholds
16:      all behind the Veil of Forgetting
17: ```
18: 
19: This is CCRPG reduced to a single sentence. Every system in the codebase exists to serve one term in this equation. The remainder of this document unpacks each term and specifies how they compose into a playable structure.
20: 
21: ### 1.1 Term definitions
22: 
23: | Term | Archetype | Game-system | Specified in |
24: |---|---|---|---|
25: | **Significator** | Hierophant (Card 5) | `PlayerProfile` — the persistent self-pattern | foundations/16 |
26: | **Great Way** | Chariot (Card 7) | The layered world of holons | foundations/18 |
27: | **Encounters** | Catalyst (Empress) → Experience (Emperor) | The atomic unit of gameplay | foundations/14, concept-drafts/ |
28: | **Choice/polarity engine** | Archetype 22 | `PolarityVector` — STO/STS crystallisation | foundations/19 |
29: | **Transformation** | Lovers (Card 6) | Stage-threshold frame-change events | foundations/17 |
30: | **Veil of Forgetting** | Embedded Unconscious | The experiential principle — no meta-awareness | foundations/20 |
31: | **64 modules** | The lesser-cycle catalyst pool | 8 lines × 8 stages, each with 7 modality games | concept-drafts/ |
32: 
33: ### 1.2 The two cycles unified
34: 
35: The lesser cycle (Matrix → Potentiator → Catalyst → Experience) operates *within* each encounter. The greater cycle (Significator → Transformation → Great Way → Choice) operates *across* the player's entire game-lifetime. This document is the bridge: it specifies how thousands of lesser-cycle encounters, drawn from the 64-module pool and delivered through 7 modalities, accumulate into the greater-cycle arc of Transformation and Choice.
36: 
37: ### 1.3 Option C: the layered-world incarnation
38: 
39: Three structural options were considered for CCRPG's world:
40: - **Option A:** 64 separate game-worlds (one per module) — rejected; no coherent narrative
41: - **Option B:** A single flat world with gated zones — rejected; no perceptual shift at Transformation
42: - **Option C:** ONE world with 8 perceptual layers — accepted; the Incarnation Architecture
43: 
44: Option C means: the player inhabits a single, continuous world. What changes at each stage transition is not the *world* but the *perception* of it. This is the Incarnation Architecture — the player is incarnated into a world they perceive through the lens of their current developmental altitude, and Transformation shifts that lens.
45:

61: | 6 | Green | Garden-lush, earth-toned, communal | Relational, ecological, interconnected | Healers, pluralists, activists, artists |
62: | 7 | Turquoise | Crystalline, vast, translucent | Holonic, multi-scale, integral | Sages, vision-logicians, planetary stewards |
63: | 8 | White | Luminous silence, minimal, spacious | Non-dual, paradox-holding | The witness, the transparent vessel |
64: 
65: ### 2.2 Layers are strata of perception, not separate maps
66: 
67: A player at Red altitude and a player at Green altitude stand in the *same* world-coordinate. They perceive different things:
68: 
69: - **NPCs visible:** Each NPC has a primary layer. An NPC whose signature is Amber is invisible (or perceived as a flat background figure) to a Red-altitude player. At Amber altitude, that NPC becomes a full interactable character with dialogue, quests, and relational depth.
70: - **Environments accessible:** Certain spaces exist only at certain layers. A meditation grove is physically present at all layers but is perceived as "empty clearing" at Red, "pleasant garden" at Green, and "crystalline sanctuary" at Turquoise.
71: - **Encounter types eligible:** The encounter scheduler only draws from modules at or below the player's current altitude (plus golden-shadow horizon encounters from one layer above).
72: - **Palette and music:** Each layer carries its ray-palette and modal audio signature (per MVP-BLUEPRINT §14–15). The renderer blends layers based on the player's perceptual state.
73: 
74: ### 2.3 Bleed-through and horizon-impression
75: 
76: The player does not perceive *only* their dominant layer. Two additional perceptual phenomena operate:
77: 
78: **Theta-decay bleed-through (downward):** When a lower layer's module has decayed (theta-decay per foundations/14), that layer *bleeds through* into the player's perception. A Turquoise player who has neglected their Red-stage health will see Red-layer elements intruding — fortress walls cracking through the crystalline landscape, aggressive NPCs appearing where none should be. This is the holonic maintenance principle made perceptual: neglected lower stages demand attention.
79: 
80: **Golden-shadow horizon (upward):** The player receives faint impressions of the *next* layer above their current altitude. These are not full interactions — they are glimpses: a distant figure that vanishes, a sound that doesn't belong, an environmental detail that seems to shimmer with unrealised meaning. These impressions are the emergent unconscious (the Potentiator) calling the Significator forward. They intensify as the player approaches a Transformation threshold.
81: 
82: ### 2.4 Transformation as perceptual layer-shift
83: 
84: At a successful Transformation event (per foundations/17), the player's dominant perceptual layer shifts. This is not a teleport or a loading screen. It is a *revelation*: the same world, perceived with new eyes. Concretely:
85: 
86: - The renderer activates the next layer's palette, lighting, and shader uniforms
87: - Previously invisible NPCs fade into visibility over 2–3 sessions
88: - Previously inaccessible spaces become navigable
89: - The audio engine shifts modal scale and instrumentation
90: - The encounter scheduler begins drawing from the new stage's modules
91: - The old layer's encounters transition to shadow-mode (maintenance, not advancement)
92: 
93: The player's felt-sense: "This was always here. I couldn't see it before."
94: 
95: ### 2.5 What "layer" means for the engine
96: 
97: Technically, a layer is a tagged set of:
98: - **Render data:** palette uniforms, shader parameters, particle systems, lighting profiles
99: - **Audio data:** modal scale, instrumentation set, ambient soundscape
100: - **Entity visibility masks:** which NPCs, objects, and environmental features are perceptible
101: - **Encounter eligibility flags:** which modules the scheduler may draw from
102: - **Physics modifiers:** movement feel, gravity weight, interaction responsiveness
103: 
104: The engine maintains all 8 layers simultaneously in data; only the active layer (plus bleed-through and horizon) is rendered. Layer transitions are gradual blends, not hard cuts.

108: ## 3. The encounter as atomic unit
109: 
110: ### 3.1 Definition
111: 
112: The **encounter** is the atomic unit of gameplay. Every moment of meaningful player engagement is an encounter. Every encounter is a lesser-cycle catalyst→experience→integration loop (per foundations/14) wrapped in narrative and delivered through a specific modality.
113: 
114: ### 3.2 Encounter identity
115: 
116: Every encounter carries a fixed identity tuple:
117: 
118: ```
119: encounter = {
120:   line:     Line,           // which of 8 lines of intelligence
121:   stage:    Stage,          // which of 8 developmental stages
122:   modality: GameModality,   // which of 7 catalyst-delivery axes
123:   holon:    HolonRef,       // which entity in the Great Way sources it
124:   role:     EncounterRole,  // side | mini | main | shadow | threshold
125:   ray:      Ray,            // canonical energy-ray binding
126:   polarity: PolarityEligibility  // which choices carry STO/STS signal
127: }
128: ```
129: 
130: No encounter exists without all six coordinates. This is the encounter's address in the game's architecture.
131: 
132: ### 3.3 The encounter contract
133: 
134: Every encounter operates a strict input→output contract:
135: 
136: **Inputs:**
137: | Input | Source | What it provides |
138: |---|---|---|
139: | Significator state | PlayerProfile (foundations/16) | Current altitudes, drive-balance, shadow-ledger, polarity vector, transformation-readiness |
140: | Holon state | Great Way world-state (foundations/18) | The sourcing entity's current altitude, shadow-state, relationship to player |
141: | Scheduler decision | Encounter scheduler (§4) | Why this encounter was selected — which need it addresses |
142: | Session context | Runtime telemetry | Player energy estimate, time available, patience signals |
143: 
144: **Outputs:**
145: | Output | Destination | What it records |
146: |---|---|---|
147: | Telemetry | Local encrypted storage | Raw behavioural data (RT, accuracy, choice patterns, engagement quality) |
148: | Consequence vector | Great Way world-state | How the encounter's outcome changes the sourcing holon and adjacent holons |
149: | Polarity vector contribution | PolarityVector on PlayerProfile | The STO/STS signal from any choice-points within the encounter |
150: | Integration signal | Distortion Ledger on PlayerProfile | Whether shadow material was surfaced, partially integrated, or fully resolved |
151: | Drive-health update | Drive weights on PlayerProfile | How the encounter shifted the player's drive-balance |
152: | Theta refresh | Task staircases on PlayerProfile | Capacity demonstration resets decay timers |
153: 
154: ### 3.4 The encounter lifecycle
155: 
156: ```
157: 1. SELECTION    — Scheduler selects encounter spec
158: 2. GENERATION   — LLM (or authored content) instantiates the encounter surface
159: 3. PRESENTATION — Game engine renders the encounter in the world
160: 4. ENGAGEMENT   — Player interacts; lesser-cycle runs (catalyst→experience)
161: 5. RESOLUTION   — Encounter concludes; outputs computed
162: 6. PROPAGATION  — Outputs written to PlayerProfile and world-state
163: 7. CHECKPOINT   — State saved; player may exit
164: ```
165: 
166: Steps 1–2 are invisible to the player. Steps 3–5 are the gameplay. Steps 6–7 are invisible. The Veil (foundations/20) ensures the player experiences only steps 3–5 as "playing the game."
167: 
168: ### 3.5 Encounter duration and the infinite checkpoint model
169: 
170: Encounters vary in duration (30 seconds to 15 minutes) but ALL support the infinite checkpoint model:
171: - The player can exit at any checkpoint within an encounter
172: - Progress within the encounter is saved
173: - The player can resume in a future session
174: - No encounter requires uninterrupted completion
175: - Session length is always player-determined
176: 
177: This is non-negotiable (per AGENTS.md §5.7).

181: ## 4. The encounter scheduler
182: 
183: > **Full algorithmic specification:** see `foundations/24-encounter-scheduler.md`. This section provides the architectural overview; doc 24 provides the implementable algorithm with priority formulas, polarity-conditioned selection modes, shadow-targeting logic, transformation-window scheduling, session-level arc management, and the macro-catalyst engine.
184: 
185: The encounter scheduler is the world's intelligence — the algorithmic engine that decides *what* encounters to present, *when*, and *why*. It is the bridge between the Significator's needs and the Great Way's offerings.
186: 
187: ### 4.1 Inputs
188: 
189: The scheduler reads three input domains:
190: 
191: **Significator state (from PlayerProfile):**
192: - Theta-decay per line (which capacities are degrading from neglect)
193: - Drive-balance (which drives are over/under-expressed)
194: - Shadow-ledger (which shadows are unresolved, which are approaching threshold)
195: - Polarity vector (current direction, magnitude, momentum)
196: - Transformation-readiness (convergence count, saturation, shadow-clearance)
197: - Per-line altitude and confidence bands
198: 
199: **World state (from Great Way):**
200: - Active holons and their current states (which NPCs/groups/organisations are in play)
201: - Current narrative beats (which story arcs are active, which are gated)
202: - PESTLE configuration (the macro-environment's current pressures per foundations/18)
203: - Holon-encounter availability (which holons have undelivered catalyst)
204: 
205: **Session context (from runtime):**
206: - Player energy estimate (derived from engagement quality, RT trends, session duration)
207: - Time available (inferred from session patterns; never asked directly)
208: - Patience signals (skip rate, pause frequency, exploration vs. goal-seeking behaviour)
209: - Recent encounter history (anti-repetition buffer)
210: 
211: ### 4.2 Decision criteria
212: 
213: The scheduler applies the following priority stack (highest first):
214: 
215: 1. **Theta-decay urgency:** If any line's capacity has decayed past the warning threshold, surface an encounter for that line at the decayed stage. The holon is never outgrown; neglect demands attention.
216: 
217: 2. **Active compound shadow:** If the shadow-ledger shows a compound shadow pattern (per module-spec §6) involving 2+ modules, surface an encounter that addresses the compound — not just one module in isolation.
218: 
219: 3. **Transformation threshold proximity:** If the Significator is approaching a Transformation threshold (per foundations/17 §2.1), enter threshold mode — surface dual-shadow encounters that address both dark (current stage) and golden (next stage) material.
220: 
221: 4. **Polarity-conditioning:** Match encounter polarity-eligibility to the player's current crystallisation phase (per foundations/19 §5). Uncrystallised players get maximum diversity; consolidating players get temptation-tests; crystallised players get deepening encounters.
222: 
223: 5. **Narrative gating:** Respect active narrative arcs. If a story beat requires a specific encounter sequence, honour it. Narrative gates override pure-algorithmic selection when active.
224: 
225: 6. **Modality rotation:** Avoid presenting the same modality consecutively. Rotate across the 6 discrete modalities; the 7th (Immersive-RPG) runs continuously as ambient.
226: 
227: 7. **Session-fit:** Match encounter duration and intensity to the player's current energy and available time. Low-energy sessions get shorter, lower-intensity encounters. High-energy sessions get catalytic peaks.
228: 
229: ### 4.3 Output
230: 
231: The scheduler produces an **encounter spec** — a data structure containing:
232: 
233: ```ts
234: interface ScheduledEncounter {
235:   moduleRef: { line: Line; stage: Stage };
236:   modality: GameModality;
237:   holonSource: HolonRef;
238:   role: EncounterRole;
239:   catalyticPurpose: 'capacity' | 'shadow' | 'drive-health' | 'threshold' | 'maintenance';
240:   polarityEligibility: PolarityEligibility;
241:   narrativeContext: NarrativeBeatRef | null;
242:   intensityTarget: number;  // 0.0–1.0
243:   durationEstimateMs: number;
244: }
245: ```
246: 
247: This spec is passed to the content generation layer (LLM or authored content lookup) for instantiation into a playable encounter surface.
248: 
249: ### 4.4 The scheduler never coerces
250: 
251: The scheduler *offers* encounters. The player *chooses* which to enter. Multiple encounter options are always available (minimum 2, typically 3–5). The player's choice of which encounter to engage is itself a signal — avoidance patterns feed back into the shadow-ledger; approach patterns confirm drive-health.
252: 
253: The scheduler respects the contact boundary (per foundations/13, foundations/14): it presents catalyst at the player's edge, never beyond it. If the player consistently avoids a category of encounter, the scheduler notes the avoidance (shadow signal) but does not force engagement. It re-presents the same catalyst in different modalities and narrative frames.

257: ## 5. Modality → encounter-type mapping
258: 
259: The 7 modalities (per foundations/11) manifest in the world as distinct encounter types. Six are **discrete** — bounded gameplay sequences with clear entry and exit. One is **ambient** — always running, always observing.
260: 
261: ### 5.1 The ambient layer: Immersive-RPG
262: 
263: The Immersive-RPG modality IS the world itself. It is not a discrete encounter the player enters and exits — it is the continuous experience of inhabiting the Great Way. Everything the player does *between* discrete encounters is Immersive-RPG:
264: 
265: - Navigation choices (where they go, what they explore, what they avoid)
266: - Spontaneous NPC interactions (greetings, observations, micro-dialogues)
267: - Environmental engagement (picking up objects, reading inscriptions, observing weather)
268: - Combat encounters (ATB fights with cognitive overlays)
269: - Resource decisions (inventory, upgrades, rest)
270: 
271: The Immersive-RPG modality is the **ecological validator** — it confirms whether capacities demonstrated in discrete encounters transfer to spontaneous behaviour. If a player shows high Moral-line scores in Scenario-Choice encounters but makes consistently cruel choices in free-play, the discrepancy is diagnostic.
272: 
273: ### 5.2 The six discrete encounter types
274: 
275: | Modality | World manifestation | Entry trigger | Duration |
276: |---|---|---|---|
277: | **Deterministic Psychometric** | Puzzle-shrines, training grounds, challenge-arenas, chase sequences | Player approaches a shrine/arena; scheduler places one in path | 3–8 min |
278: | **Language-Reflective** | Campfire journals, altar prayers, mentor dialogues, dream-sequences | Player rests at a campfire; visits an altar; sleeps | 2–10 min |
279: | **Scenario-Choice** | NPC encounters with branching dialogue, moral dilemmas, faction negotiations | NPC approaches player; player enters a settlement; story beat triggers | 3–12 min |
280: | **Embodied-Somatic** | Rhythmic combat, breath-gated abilities, posture challenges, dance-rituals | Combat encounter; ritual site; physical challenge in environment | 2–8 min |
281: | **Strategic-Planning** | Siege planning, expedition preparation, resource allocation, territory management | War-room entry; expedition launch; faction leadership moment | 5–15 min |
282: | **Social-Cooperative** | Group missions with NPC parties, faction politics, council debates, teaching moments | Party formation; council summons; NPC requests aid | 5–15 min |
283: 
284: ### 5.3 How discrete encounters arise in the world
285: 
286: Discrete encounters do not appear as menu selections or UI prompts. They arise *within* the Immersive-RPG layer as natural world-events:
287: 
288: - A puzzle-shrine glows as the player passes (Deterministic)
289: - A companion sits by a fire and asks "What are you thinking?" (Language-Reflective)
290: - A stranger blocks the path with a demand (Scenario-Choice)
291: - A drumbeat begins and enemies appear in rhythm (Embodied-Somatic)
292: - A war-council convenes and the player is asked to plan (Strategic-Planning)
293: - An NPC party needs a leader for a dangerous mission (Social-Cooperative)
294: 
295: The transition from ambient to discrete is seamless. The player experiences "something happened in the world" — not "I entered a mini-game." The Veil is maintained.
296: 
297: ### 5.4 Modality-shadow affinity
298: 
299: Each modality has natural strengths for surfacing specific shadow material (per concept-drafts/README §Cross-Validation Logic):
300: 
301: | Modality | Surfaces most clearly |
302: |---|---|
303: | Deterministic | Capacity ceiling; dark-allergy (avoidance); golden-addiction (self-selected difficulty gap) |
304: | Language-Reflective | Metacognitive depth; golden-addiction (verbal performance without substrate) |
305: | Scenario-Choice | Value structure; moral stage; polarity orientation |
306: | Embodied-Somatic | Body-mind integration; somatic dark-allergy; willpower pathology |
307: | Strategic-Planning | Executive function; agency pathology; eros compulsion (over-planning) |
308: | Social-Cooperative | Interpersonal capacity; communion pathology; agency isolation |
309: | Immersive-RPG | Ecological transfer; spontaneous drive expression; compound shadows |
310: 
311: The scheduler uses these affinities when selecting modality: if the catalytic purpose is "shadow surfacing for dark-allergy on Cognitive/Red," the scheduler preferentially selects Deterministic modality (which surfaces that shadow most clearly).

315: ## 6. The 3-act macro-structure
316: 
317: The narrative architecture (per narrative/00) maps onto the layered world as three acts, each spanning specific perceptual layers and carrying distinct developmental themes.
318: 
319: ### 6.1 Act I — The Embodied World (Infrared, Magenta)
320: 
321: **Theme:** "I am alive. I imagine."
322: 
323: The player learns to perceive the world. The Significator is nascent — drive-profile forming, line-altitudes differentiating, first shadows surfacing. The world is primal: cave-lit, dream-saturated, symbol-rich.
324: 
325: **Structural role:**
326: - Onboarding and calibration (per MVP-BLUEPRINT §9–13)
327: - Significator initialisation — the PlayerProfile takes shape
328: - First companions gained (the animal/maternal figure, the dream-mentor)
329: - First encounter with the contact boundary — learning that the world responds to attention
330: - Polarity vector begins accumulating (first micro-choices, low weight)
331: 
332: **Transformation I→II:** The player is *named* — speaks their first words, chooses their first symbol, takes their first stand. Perception shifts from Infrared/Magenta layers to Red. The world sharpens from dream into force.
333: 
334: ### 6.2 Act II — The World of Selves (Red, Amber, Orange, Green)
335: 
336: **Theme:** "Who am I, with whom, why?"
337: 
338: The bulk of gameplay. The player becomes a *self* — first as warrior (Red), then as tradition-member (Amber), then as rational individual (Orange), then as sensitive pluralist (Green). Each stage's layer reveals new dimensions of the same world.
339: 
340: **Structural role:**
341: - Four full Transformation events (Red→Amber, Amber→Orange, Orange→Green, Green→Turquoise)
342: - Four major antagonists, each embodying a stage-fixation (per narrative/00 §4.2):
343:   - The Conqueror (Red × Agency-fixation)
344:   - The Inquisitor (Amber × Communion-fixation)
345:   - The Architect (Orange × Eros-fixation)
346:   - The Equivocator (Green × Agape-fixation)
347: - The central tension: *the seductiveness of each stage*. Each layer is beautiful, meaningful, and complete-feeling. The player is tempted to stay. The antagonists embody this temptation.
348: - Polarity vector consolidates and begins crystallising. By late Green, most players have entered the consolidation phase (magnitude 0.3–0.6).
349: - All 8 lines exercised across all 4 stages = 32 modules of content
350: 
351: **Transformation events within Act II** follow the full Lovers Crucible pattern (per foundations/17 §2.2): Unravelling → Crucible → Emergence. Each transition costs the player something they valued at the previous stage. Each transition reveals something that was always present but imperceptible.
352: 
353: ### 6.3 Act III — The World of Wholes (Turquoise, White)
354: 
355: **Theme:** "Who am I, when 'I' is one of many holons in a larger field?"
356: 
357: The integral and non-dual stages. The world becomes spacious — fewer encounters, deeper each. The narrative quiets. The player's *self* is transcended-and-included into larger holons.
358: 
359: **Structural role:**
360: - Two final Transformation events (Turquoise→White, White→Harvest)
361: - The Choice crystallises — polarity vector reaches locked phase (magnitude ≥ 0.85)
362: - The protagonist's future self appears as mentor at Turquoise threshold
363: - The protagonist *authors* their closing reflection at White (player-written text)
364: - The harvest endgame (post-White) — transition into 4th density (per MVP-BLUEPRINT §16)
365: - The world renders with maximum perceptual depth — all 8 layers simultaneously visible to the integral perceiver
366: 
367: **Transformation at Act III's close:** The final Transformation is not into a new stage but into a new *density*. The Significator's game-lifetime concludes. The character is retired; the psychograph preserved; the player's words become part of the world (multiplayer: mentor presence for other players).
368: 
369: ### 6.4 How Transformation events bridge acts and stages
370: 
371: Each Transformation event is both a narrative climax and a mechanical phase-transition:
372: 
373: | Transition | Narrative beat | Mechanical shift |
374: |---|---|---|
375: | Infrared → Magenta | The first dream; the world responds to symbol | Layer 2 activates; symbol-based encounters unlock |
376: | Magenta → Red | The naming; the first stand | Layer 3 activates; combat system fully online |
377: | Red → Amber | The surrender of dominance; joining a tradition | Layer 4 activates; rule-based encounters unlock |
378: | Amber → Orange | The questioning; breaking from dogma | Layer 5 activates; rational/strategic encounters unlock |
379: | Orange → Green | The opening; feeling the other | Layer 6 activates; relational/ecological encounters unlock |
380: | Green → Turquoise | The integration; seeing the whole spiral | Layer 7 activates; integral encounters unlock |
381: | Turquoise → White | The silence; releasing the need to integrate | Layer 8 activates; non-dual encounters unlock |
382: | White → Harvest | The authoring; the player's final words | All layers unified; game-lifetime concludes |

455: - The modality contracts

463: | Drop | Stages | Content volume |

465: | MVP | Red (full) + Infrared (prologue) | 8 modules × 7 games + narrative arc |
